questions.q: How does adding a region to a Cosmos DB account compare to setting up a secondary SQL Server replica in another datacenter?
options: It's a configuration change (portal, CLI, or API) that triggers automatic background replication, not a manual infrastructure project
It requires manually seeding the new region with a backup file
It requires rebuilding the entire account from scratch
Regions cannot be added after an account is created
questions.explain: Global distribution is a property of the Cosmos DB account itself — adding a region is a few clicks or an API call, with the engine handling replication automatically.

questions.q: In the default single-region write mode, how do non-write regions behave?
options: They serve as read replicas kept automatically in sync, with automatic failover if the write region fails
They reject all traffic until manually promoted
They accept writes but not reads
They are deleted automatically after 30 days
questions.explain: Single-region write designates exactly one write region; the others are synced read replicas that can be promoted via failover priority.

questions.q: What does enabling multi-region writes (multi-master) actually change?
options: Every configured region can accept writes simultaneously, reducing write latency for geographically distributed applications
It disables all read replicas
It converts the account into a single-region deployment
It removes the need for a partition key
questions.explain: Multi-region writes let an application write to its nearest region instead of round-tripping to a single designated write region.

questions.q: What real problem does multi-region writes introduce that single-region write mode never has?
options: The possibility of conflicting writes to the same item made in different regions before replication catches up
Higher write latency for every application
The complete loss of read availability
The requirement to disable the change feed
questions.explain: With only one writer (single-region write), conflicts are impossible; multi-region writes make them possible because two regions can modify the same item near-simultaneously.

questions.q: What does 'failover priority' control in a Cosmos DB account?
options: The order in which regions are promoted to become the write region if the current write region fails
The order in which regions are billed
Which region gets the fastest read performance regardless of location
The order documents are indexed in
questions.explain: Failover priority determines which region becomes the new write region during an automatic failover in single-region write mode.
